seoTitle: Error Level Analysis (ELA) for JPEG Photos
metaDescription: Recompress a JPEG at a fixed quality and show the amplified difference, so areas that were edited or pasted in may stand out. A hint for review, not proof...
intro: Highlight regions that may have been edited in a JPEG.
why:
The photo is saved again as a JPEG at a set quality, and the difference from the original is amplified and shown as a picture. Regions with a different save history can look brighter or darker than the rest.

This is a hint, not proof. Edges, text, saturated colours and noise glow on their own, and screenshots or heavily re-saved files give confusing maps. Use it to decide where to look, then look.
howTo: Look for areas that differ from their surroundings.

faq.q: Can it prove a photo is fake?
faq.a: No. It can point at places worth a closer look.
90 is a common start. Try 75 to 95.
It runs, but the map is not meaningful for lossless files.
No. The work happens in your browser and the page makes no network request with your input.
